title: Ancient Rituals, Distant Landscapes
program_note: Ancient myths from many cultures are often filled with images of both incomparable beauty and unimaginable pain.  Some of the pain and agony result from failure to perform proper rituals—as with Adam and Eve and their banishment from the Garden of Eden, or with Izanagi and Izanami, the birth of Ebisu, and later Izanami’s death.  Sometimes the rituals demanded are too horrible actually to perform—as with Abraham, Sarah, and the sacrifice of Isaac—while other times the horror of those rituals only indirectly results in further unhappiness—as with Theseus and his abandonment of Ariadne.  This work of music is meant to portray some of the unreal beauty of such mythic places as the Garden of Eden (the “Distant Landscapes”), contrasted with the fearsomeness, awe, and dread of those “Ancient Rituals”.  To that end, at times the performer is instructed to speak or whisper certain syllables; some of these syllables have meaning while some do not—all of them, however, are meant to sound ominous and threatening.
